lessons.title: I'm hungry
lessons.canDo: Say you are hungry or thirsty.
lessons.scenario: Smarty is hungry and thirsty in the kitchen. Mia gives him water, bread and an apple.

items.note: Say 'I am hungry' when you want to eat.

image.describe: a thin cat with a rumbling tummy staring at an empty bowl

items.note: Say 'I am thirsty' when you want to drink something.

image.describe: a cat with its tongue out looking at a tall empty glass

items.note: Water is the clear drink we all need every day.

image.describe: a cat pouring clear water from a jug into a glass

items.note: Say 'bread' for the food we cut into slices and eat at meals.

image.describe: a cat holding a fresh loaf of bread with slices on a board

items.note: Say 'apple' for one round fruit; more than one is 'apples'.

image.describe: a cat proudly holding a big red apple

practice.prompt: Look at a cat with an empty glass. How does it feel?
practice.explanation: Thirsty is for drinks; hungry is for food.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Hungry means you want to eat.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: I am thirsty means you want a drink.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about the fruit.
Match the feeling or word to its partner.
practice.explanation: Hungry goes with bread, thirsty with water, and one apple becomes apples.

practice.prompt: Say it aloud. You can try again.
practice.explanation: You said you want to eat.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks about a drink.
practice.explanation: Are you thirsty? asks about a feeling.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Apple comes after I have an.

image.describe: The kitchen: Smarty the black cat sits at the table while Mia puts a glass of water, bread and a red apple in front of him.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes, I am. I am thirsty, too.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I have bread and an apple.

questions.explanation: Smarty says: I am hungry.

questions.prompt: What is the drink on the table?
questions.explanation: Mia says: This is water.

questions.prompt: Who has bread and an apple?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I have bread and an apple.

mission.setup: You are in the kitchen with Smarty. Say how you feel and say thank you.

turns.hint: Say yes and use the word hungry.
Say yes and use the word thirsty.

turns.smarty: This is water. This is bread. Say thank you.

lessons.title: Breakfast
lessons.scenario: Mia and Sam make breakfast. Smarty learns the words for morning food and drinks.

items.note: 'Breakfast' is the first meal of the day, in the morning.

image.describe: a cat at a kitchen table with a plate of breakfast and a sunrise window

items.note: Say 'egg' for one and 'eggs' for more than one.

image.describe: a cat carefully holding a white egg next to a frying pan

items.note: Say 'milk' for the white drink that comes from cows.

image.describe: a kitten drinking milk from a small saucer

items.note: Say 'tea' for the hot drink made with leaves.

image.describe: a cat holding a steaming cup of tea

items.note: Say 'coffee' for the dark hot drink many people like in the morning.

image.describe: a sleepy cat holding a steaming mug of coffee

items.example: I have an egg for breakfast.
items.note: Use 'for' to say what you have at a meal: for breakfast.

practice.prompt: Which word is the morning meal?
practice.explanation: Breakfast is the meal in the morning.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: An egg starts with a vowel sound, so we say an egg.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: We use for to say the meal.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
Match one thing to many things.
practice.explanation: Add s to make most words plural.

practice.prompt: Which drink is white?
Say it aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: I have an egg for breakfast.
practice.answer: I have an egg for breakfast.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
options: Milk and an apple for breakfast.
practice.explanation: Tea and coffee are hot morning drinks.

image.describe: The kitchen in the morning: Mia, Sam and Smarty sit at a table with eggs, bread, milk, tea and coffee.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning, Mia. I am hungry.

questions.prompt: What does Mia have for Smarty?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I have milk for you.
Sam says: I have tea and coffee.
We say eggs for breakfast.

mission.setup: It is morning in the kitchen. Tell Smarty what you have for breakfast.

turns.smarty: Good morning! What do you have for breakfast?
turns.example: I have an egg for breakfast.

turns.smarty: Say: I have tea and coffee.

lessons.title: Do you like bananas?
lessons.scenario: Ben asks Smarty which food he likes and which food he does not like.

items.note: Ask 'Do you like...?' to find out if someone enjoys a food.
Say 'I do not like' (or 'I don't like') when you do not enjoy something.
Say 'banana' for one yellow fruit; more than one is 'bananas'.

image.describe: a cat holding a long yellow banana

items.note: Say 'cheese' for the yellow food made from milk.

image.describe: a cat sitting next to a big yellow wedge of cheese with holes

items.note: Use 'or' to offer a choice between two things.

practice.prompt: Ask a friend if they enjoy cheese.
practice.explanation: Do you like...? asks about likes.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: I do not like says something is not enjoyable.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start the question with Do you like.

practice.prompt: Offer a choice.
Match one to many.
practice.explanation: Add s for many; cheese stays the same.

practice.prompt: Say you do not enjoy cheese.
practice.explanation: I do not like says no.

practice.prompt: Say it aloud. You can try again.
Smarty asks about milk. Answer yes.
practice.text: Do you like milk? Yes, I ___.
practice.explanation: We answer Do you like with Yes, I do.

practice.prompt: Say you enjoy apples.

story.hook: What food does Smarty not like?

image.describe: The kitchen: Ben shows Smarty a bunch of bananas, a block of cheese, a jug of milk and a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: No, I do not like cheese.

questions.prompt: Ben asks: Do you like bananas? Smarty says: ___, I do.
questions.explanation: Smarty answers yes to bananas.
Smarty says: I do not like cheese.
Smarty says: Milk, please.

mission.setup: Ben asks about food. Answer with what you like and do not like.

turns.example: No, I do not like cheese.
turns.hint: Say you like it or do not like it.

lessons.title: Lunch and dinner
lessons.scenario: Leo tells Smarty about lunch and dinner.

items.note: 'Lunch' is the meal in the middle of the day.

image.describe: a cat eating lunch under a bright midday sun

items.note: 'Dinner' is the main meal in the evening.

image.describe: a family of cats at a dinner table at night with candles

items.note: Say 'rice' for the small white grains we cook and eat.

image.describe: a cat with a bowl of white rice and a spoon

items.note: Say 'soup' for the warm food you eat with a spoon.

image.describe: a cat blowing on a steaming bowl of soup

items.note: Say 'chicken' for the bird we cook and eat.

image.describe: a cat next to a roast chicken on a plate

practice.prompt: Which meal is in the evening?
Listen, then choose what you heard.
Build the sentence.
Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Soup is a food for dinner.

practice.prompt: Match the meal to the time.
practice.explanation: Breakfast is morning, lunch is afternoon, dinner is evening.

practice.prompt: Say it aloud. You can try again.
Say you do not like rice.
practice.explanation: I do not like says no.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.

story.hook: What is for lunch and dinner?

image.describe: The kitchen: Leo puts chicken and rice on one table and soup and bread on another while Smarty watches.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! Do you like chicken?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Yes, I do! I like rice, too.

questions.explanation: Leo says: Lunch is chicken and rice.
Leo says: Dinner is soup and bread.

questions.prompt: Who asks: Do you like chicken?
questions.explanation: Leo asks the question.

mission.setup: Leo talks about lunch and dinner. Answer his questions.

turns.smarty: It is lunch. Do you like chicken?
What do you have for lunch?

lessons.title: Can I have juice?
lessons.scenario: Sam and Smarty ask Mia politely for juice and cake.

items.note: Say 'Can I have...?' to ask for something politely.
Say 'juice' for the sweet drink made from fruit.

image.describe: a cat pouring bright juice into a glass with a straw

items.note: Say 'cake' for a sweet food for a party; more than one is 'cakes'.

image.describe: a cat next to a big birthday cake with candles

items.example: Can I have cake? Of course!
items.note: Say 'Of course' to answer yes in a friendly way.
Say 'Here you are' when you give something to someone.

practice.prompt: Ask politely for juice.
practice.explanation: Can I have... is a polite question.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
Build the question.
Complete what you say when you give something.
Match one to many.
A friend asks: Can I have an apple? Say yes.
Say it aloud. You can try again.
Ask for tea.
practice.explanation: The question is Can I have.

story.hook: What do Sam and Smarty ask for?

image.describe: The kitchen: Mia gives a glass of juice to Sam and a slice of cake to Smarty, and both smile.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Of course. Here you are, Smarty.

questions.explanation: Sam says: Can I have juice, please?
Mia gives the juice and says Here you are.
Smarty says: Can I have cake?

mission.setup: Ask Mia for food politely and answer her.

turns.smarty: I have juice and cake. What do you say?

turns.hint: Say yes and give the cake.

lessons.title: Fruit and vegetables
lessons.scenario: Ana shows Smarty fruit and vegetables in the kitchen.

items.note: Say 'orange' for the round orange fruit; more than one is 'oranges'.

image.describe: a cat holding a bright orange fruit

items.note: Say 'tomato' for the round red food; more than one is 'tomatoes'.

image.describe: a cat sniffing a round red tomato

items.note: Say 'potato' for the brown food we boil or cook; more than one is 'potatoes'.

image.describe: a cat sitting next to a big brown potato

items.note: Say 'carrot' for the long orange vegetable.

image.describe: a cat holding a long orange carrot with green leaves

items.note: Say 'fruit' for sweet food like apples, bananas and oranges.

practice.prompt: Which one is a fruit?

Build the sentence.
Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Potatoes are a food for dinner.

practice.prompt: Match one to many.
practice.explanation: Words with o often add es.

practice.prompt: Say it aloud. You can try again.
Say you do not like carrots.
practice.explanation: I do not like says no.

practice.prompt: Apples and bananas are fruit. Which one is not fruit?

lines.speaker: Ana

lessons.title: Delicious!
lessons.scenario: Tom and Smarty try food that is hot, cold and sweet.

items.note: Say 'delicious' when food tastes very good.

image.describe: a cat closing its eyes happily while eating a spoonful of soup

items.note: Say 'hot' for food or drink with a high temperature.

image.describe: a cat blowing on a steaming bowl with steam rising

items.note: Say 'cold' for food or drink that is not warm.

image.describe: a cat holding a frosty glass of cold milk with ice

items.note: Say 'sweet' for food with sugar, like cake.

image.describe: a cat licking pink icing from a sweet cupcake

items.example: The tea is hot, but I like it.
items.note: Use 'but' to show a different idea: hot, but delicious.

practice.prompt: Choose the word for a very good taste.
practice.explanation: Delicious means very good to eat.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
Build the sentence.
Match the opposites.
Complete the sentence.
practice.text: I like tea, ___ I do not like coffee.

practice.prompt: Say it aloud. You can try again.
practice.text: It is hot, but it is delicious.
practice.answer: It is hot, but it is delicious.

practice.prompt: Say that the milk is cold.
practice.explanation: Cold is the opposite of hot.

practice.prompt: Do you like soup? Say how it tastes.

image.describe: The kitchen: Tom puts a steaming bowl of soup, a cold glass of milk and a sweet cake in front of Smarty.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: It is hot, but it is delicious!

questions.prompt: The soup is hot, but it is ___.
questions.explanation: Smarty says: It is hot, but it is delicious!
Tom says: The milk is cold.
Smarty says: The cake is sweet.

mission.setup: Tom gives you food. Say how it tastes.

turns.smarty: The tea is hot. Is it delicious?

items.note: Say 'cut' when you use a knife on food.

lessons.title: Some and any
lessons.scenario: Smarty asks Mia for juice and cake and learns some, any and kitchen things.

items.example: I have a cup of tea.

items.note: Say 'glass' for the tall thing we use for water or juice.

image.describe: a cat holding a tall glass of water

practice.prompt: Choose the tall thing for water.

Use the word for not.

lessons.title: Feed Smarty
lessons.canDo: Offer food and say you are full.

Say 'fish' for the animal from the sea that we cook and eat.

items.note: Say 'sandwich' for bread with food inside; more than one is 'sandwiches'.

image.describe: a cat holding a big sandwich with lettuce

items.note: Say 'I am full' when you cannot eat any more.
Use 'very' before a word to make it stronger: very hungry.

practice.explanation: Full means you cannot eat more.
